decisions.decision: Correcting the record: the wave-complete and T7 notes claimed 'openspec validate --strict passes' before that command had actually been read. It was FAILING at the time.
decisions.why: The spec delta's SHALL sat on the second wrapped line and the validator only reads the first. Reworded so SHALL leads; it now genuinely passes. The false claim is left visible here rather than quietly edited away.

decisions.decision: R1 ACCEPTED and fixed even though the reviewer filed it as minor/non-blocking: the configured-location fixture moves from America/Bogota to America/New_York.
decisions.why: Bogota is now also the fallback, so the test discriminated only via pointer identity — correct but invisible to a reader. A differing zone makes the assertion self-evident and survives anyone later 'simplifying' it.

review.brief: Validate the dateOnly→clock.CalendarDay swap is behavior-neutral (byte-identical formula), the Config.Clock/Config.Location test seams survive with only the nil-fallback target changed, the 47 repointed test call sites carry identical arguments/expected values, judge TestService_Location_UsesConfiguredLocation's pointer-identity discrimination now that its configured zone equals the fallback zone, confirm the Config.Location doc comment does not overclaim app/Scheduler's (unmigrated) state, confirm scope (no migration/cmd/clock edits, sqlc regen comment-only), confirm no new test functions beyond repairs, anti-gaming, and confirm the D23 openspec-validate correction is genuine.

findings.note: dedupe_test.go:83-94 TestService_Location_UsesConfiguredLocation loads its 'configured' fixture via time.LoadLocation("America/Bogota") — now the same IANA zone as location()'s fallback (clock.Zone(), also America/Bogota). The test still correctly discriminates: verified independently that Go's time.LoadLocation returns a fresh *Location per call (not a cached singleton) for a named zone, so got != loc still fails if location() wrongly ignores Config.Location and returns clock.Zone()'s cached pointer instead. Not a bug, not weakened — but a reader can no longer tell at a glance that the assertion discriminates 'configured' from 'default' without knowing that LoadLocation-vs-cached-Zone() implementation detail. Suggest (non-blocking): a one-line comment noting the pointer-identity reliance, or swap the fixture to a visibly different zone (e.g. America/New_York) so the discrimination reads as obvious again. Leave-to-leader's judgment; not required before archive.
